title: One cost function, three market structures
summary: The synthesizing example C(Q) = 125 + 4Q² worked as a price taker, a monopolist and a monopolistically competitive firm, and the session's conclusion.

chunks.heading: The set-up and the price taker
chunks.explanation_md:
One cost function, **C(Q) = 125 + 4Q²**, worked under three market structures. MC is the same in every case, **MC = 8Q\**, because cost does not depend on the market.

First case: you are a **price taker\** and the market price is **$40**.
chunks.exam_line: Price taker at $40: Q = 5, profit -$25, expect exit.

check_questions.stem: As a price taker at $40, the firm's profit is:

chunks.big_idea: Same cost function, but as a price taker at $40 the firm loses $25.

worked.question_md: C(Q) = 125 + 4Q². You are a price taker and other firms charge $40. Find output, profit and the implication.

steps.title: P = MC
steps.why: A price taker sets P = MC.

steps.title: Implication
steps.body_md: The firm is making a loss, so **expect exit in the long run\**.
steps.why: Losses push firms out of a competitive market.

worked.answer_md: Q = 5, profit = **-$25**: expect exit in the long run.

watch_out: MC = 8Q, not 4Q: bring the power down and multiply.
chunks.exam_answer_md: MC = 8Q. MR = P = $40; 40 = 8Q, so **Q = 5**. C(5) = 125 + 100 = $225; revenue = (40)(5) = $200; **profit = -$25**. Implication: expect exit in the long run.

chunks.heading: Monopoly or monopolistic competition
chunks.explanation_md:
Facing **P = 100 - Q**:

- **MR = 100 - 2Q**; set 100 - 2Q = 8Q, so **Q = 10**
- **P = 100 - 10 = $90**
- Profit = (90)(10) - (125 + 4(100)) = **$375**

**Implications:** a **monopolist** will not face entry unless patents or other barriers are removed. A **monopolistically competitive** firm should expect others to **clone** its product, so **profits decline over time**.
chunks.exam_line: P = 100 - Q: Q = 10, P = $90, profit $375; monopoly keeps it, monopolistic competition loses it to clones.

worked.question_md: C(Q) = 125 + 4Q² and inverse demand P = 100 - Q. Find output, price, profit and the implications for a monopolist and a monopolistically competitive firm.

steps.title: MR = MC
steps.why: Profit is highest where MR = MC.

steps.title: Implications
steps.body_md: **Monopolist:** no entry unless patents or other barriers go, so profit lasts. **Monopolistically competitive firm:** expect rivals to **clone\** the product, so profit **declines over time\**.
steps.result: Barriers keep profit; free entry erodes it

worked.answer_md: Q = 10, P = $90, profit = **$375**. The monopolist keeps it; the monopolistic competitor's profit declines as rivals clone.

watch_out: Set MR equal to **8Q**, not to 8.
The numbers are the same for monopoly and monopolistic competition; only the **long-run implication** differs.
chunks.exam_answer_md: MR = 100 - 2Q; MC = 8Q. 100 - 2Q = 8Q, so **Q = 10**; P = 100 - 10 = **$90**. Profit = (90)(10) - (125 + 4(100)) = **$375**. A monopolist will not face entry unless patents or other barriers are eliminated; a monopolistically competitive firm should expect others to clone its product, so profits decline over time.

questions.stem: In the synthesizing example, why should the price taker expect exit in the long run?

A firm has C(Q) = 125 + 4Q². Find the profit-maximizing output, price and profit if (a) it is a price taker and other firms charge $40, and (b) it is a monopolist facing P = 100 - Q. Discuss the implications.
questions.model_answer_md:
**MC = 8Q** in both cases.

**(a) Price taker:** MR = P = 40 = 8Q, so **Q = 5**. Cost = 125 + 100 = $225, revenue = $200, profit = **-$25**. Expect **exit** in the long run.

**(b) Monopoly:** MR = 100 - 2Q = 8Q, so **Q = 10**, **P = $90**. Profit = 900 - (125 + 400) = **$375**. A monopolist faces no entry unless its barriers are removed; a monopolistically competitive firm with the same demand would see rivals clone it and profits decline.
